channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: The Fifty: 50 Billboards 50 States · VSCO
item.description: Nationwide open call selecting fifty US-based photographers — one from every state — to have their work printed on billboards across the country, licensed and paid for by VSCO. No entry fee. Open to photographers aged 18 and over residing in the United States. Entries are made by posting work to a VSCO account tagged #TheFifty plus the hashtag for the photographer's state (e.g. #OHIO), with a short caption about the image or series and the state added to the profile bio; 3–5 images from a cohesive series are recommended. VSCO's curation team reviews every submission and notifies selected photographers on a rolling basis, with announcements published on the VSCO journal. Selected work may also be carried into editorial features, curation and further licensing opportunities. Billboard formats vary by state, and selected work may instead be shown through alternative large-format displays, posters or public installations. Photographs including recognisable people require a model release, and selected photographers must supply a high-resolution file suitable for large-format printing. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Billboard exhibition + paid licensing.

item.title: Photographer in Residence 2027 · Worthless Studios
item.description: One-month analog photography residency inside a 1973 Airstream trailer converted into a fully equipped black-and-white darkroom, parked at partner sites across the five boroughs of New York City. Seven artists are selected for 2027, one per month from April to October, each receiving 24/7 access to the Airstream darkroom for four weeks, a $1,500 artist stipend, free film, paper and chemistry, two free workshops on scanning and digital printing with Brooklyn PrintWorks, press packet materials and the option to host a public program. Host partners include Alice Austen House, Inspiration Point, The Green-Wood Cemetery, The Center for Arts and Advocacy, The Lower Eastside Girls Club and NYC Parks; residents may also propose their own site. Applicants need prior independent darkroom experience, must commit a minimum of 20 hours a week in the Airstream, and cannot be enrolled in — or about to enter — an art-related degree program. Applications are free and made through SlideRoom. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,500 stipend + darkroom, film and materials.

item.title: Photo Fringe 2026 — Feedback Loop
item.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led registered charity that has run an open-platform photography festival on a DIY, collectively-funded model since 2003. Registration is now open for the 2026 edition, which runs 2–31 October across Brighton & Hove, Portsmouth and Newhaven with launch events on Friday 2 October. Anyone can take part: artists, photographers, collectives, curators and organisations register their own self-curated exhibition and are then listed in the official festival programme and on photofringe.org, given marketing resources and exhibitor guidance, and folded into a city-wide trail that helps audiences find the work. Exhibitors are responsible for finding and managing their own venue, though the festival shares venue leads and connects artists looking for larger shared spaces; online-only exhibitions are equally welcome, and Photo Fringe events such as artist talks, workshops and photo walks are listed free. The 2026 theme is Feedback Loop — a cycle of action and response, thinking about how images circulate and change as they are seen, shared, interpreted and reworked, and what becomes possible when work is made with others rather than alone. Responding to the theme is encouraged but not compulsory. Contributions towards the festival are £125 for a solo exhibition at a venue and online, £150 for a group exhibition, £60 for solo online-only and £100 for group online-only, all subsidised; a small number of bursaries are available for exhibitors who cannot afford a contribution, by emailing the festival. All registered exhibitors are automatically entered for the Danny Wilson Memorial Awards, supported by Photoworks, whose prizes include a bursary, mentoring sessions and artist talks. Registration closes 1 September 2026. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: £125 solo / £150 group (online-only £60 / £100); bursaries available. Prize: Exhibition + Bursary.

item.title: Shrode Photography Competition and Exhibit 2026 · Cedarhurst Center for the Arts
item.description: Cedarhurst Center for the Arts is an AAM-accredited museum and sculpture park in Mount Vernon, Illinois, and its annual Shrode Photography Competition is a juried competition and exhibition for photographic film and digital photographs. Cedarhurst invites an established photography professional to judge; after viewing each digital entry individually the judge selects the works accepted into the exhibition and the top awards. Work must be the entrant's original work made within the past three years (2023 or later) and not previously shown in a Cedarhurst or Shrode Art Center competition or exhibition. Submissions may carry an inconspicuous watermark for judging, but accepted photographs must be printed watermark-free and a clean digital file supplied for marketing use. Each artist may submit up to two entry forms at $25 each ($20 for Cedarhurst members), three photographs per form, for a maximum of six photographs judged. All submissions are digital — JPEG or TIFF, each file named with the artist's last name and entry number — and must be received by 5pm on Wednesday 26 August 2026; images on a non-returnable USB flash drive are also accepted. Accepted artists are emailed by the end of the day on 2 September 2026, and accepted work, framed and wired for hanging, must arrive at Shrode Art Center by 25 September. The exhibition runs 4 October 2026 – 10 January 2027 with an awards reception on Saturday 3 October, and closes with an Art Chat hosted by Shrode Art Center director Carrie Stover on 10 January. Awards are Best of Show $500, 1st Place $250, 2nd Place $200 and a People's Choice Award of $100 announced at the close of the show, with honorable mention certificates at the judge's discretion. Entry is open to artists 18 and older living south of Interstate 70, including the Charleston, Illinois area. — Deadline: August 26, 2026. Fee: $25 for up to 3 photos ($20 members). Prize: $500 / $250 / $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: Out of Shape · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Out of Shape celebrates unconventional forms, irregular edges and artwork that moves beyond the traditional rectangle. The gallery is looking for work that treats shape as both a compositional element and a physical object — shaped supports, abstracted forms, irregular compositions, unconventional framing, sculptural wall pieces and other inventive approaches to form, whether organic or geometric, subtle or dramatic. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking, provided the work engages with the theme through form, structure or presentation. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 12 September 2026. — Deadline: August 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Uncanny · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Uncanny explores the eerie, the mysterious and the unexplainable, and welcomes artwork that embraces the strange, surreal and unsettling — haunting figures, dreamlike landscapes, cryptic symbolism, eerie atmospheres and imagined creatures. Whether psychological, supernatural, grotesque or quietly unsettling, the gallery is after work that evokes curiosity, tension and wonder and invites viewers into worlds that defy explanation. Photography and digital media are named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 10 October 2026. — Deadline: September 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Less Is More · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Less Is More is a small-works exhibition open to pieces 12 x 12 inches or smaller, built around the idea that size does not limit presence, meaning or visual impact. The gallery is interested in the experience of engaging with work on an intimate scale, where every piece has the chance to command attention and invite closer observation. Photography and digital media are named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 14 November 2026. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Semioculus XXIII
item.description: Semioculus is an independent international art zine and artist community originally founded in Tartu, Estonia, grown from a hobby project started by a group of college course mates into an international community and published quarterly in digital and limited print runs, dedicated to dark and surreal work from around the world — its own aesthetic keywords are dark, dreamlike, macabre, obscure and surreal. Submissions are open for the twenty-third issue, and the guidelines set no theme beyond that aesthetic: artists are free to send new pieces or older work, provided the publication rights still belong to them. Self-published work and images previously posted to an artist's own website or social media are fine. Any medium that can be published both digitally and in print is accepted as long as it fits the aesthetic; AI-generated work and fan art of any kind are not accepted. Visual art should be sent as JPG, PDF, TIFF or PNG at the highest resolution possible and no lower than 200 DPI, no more than six pieces at a time, with filenames formatted ArtistName_TitleOfWork; poems and flash fiction are also accepted, up to six A5 pages. Submissions are taken by email only, with the artist's name, titles, an optional short text tied to the work and a link to a website or social media in the body of the message. The zine is run as a passion project and cannot currently offer artists payment — it is free to enter, the original artist retains all rights to their work, and selected artists are contacted within one to two weeks of the deadline. Only artists aged 18 and up are accepted, as the zine occasionally features mature themes. Submissions close 16 August 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: GO GREEN · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on the colour green — which sits at the psychological midpoint of the spectrum and is processed by the eye with the least strain of any hue, tied to safety, stability and growth but just as able to tip into envy or unease. The organisers call that range one of the more emotionally loaded colours an artist can work with, and want your version of it. Open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, photography named explicitly among them; work previously selected for an Art Fluent exhibit is not eligible and AI will not be accepted. Curated and juried by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill with an anonymous committee — there is no personal feedback from jurors. Best of Show takes $750 and two Director's Choice awards take $250 each; all accepted pieces are shown in the online gallery at art-fluent.com. JPEGs are due by midnight MST on November 20, 2026, with notification and the gallery opening by December 18. Entry is $25 for the first piece and $10 for each additional, up to twenty. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $1,250.

item.title: 2026 National Juried Show · Washington Art Association
item.description: The Washington Art Association & Gallery's national juried show, open to artists across the United States and juried by the New York painter Barbara Grossman, who studied at Cooper Union and the Akademie der Künste in Munich and has taught at the Yale School of Art, the New York Studio School and Chautauqua. Original photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, works on paper (drawing, watercolour, printmaking, collage) and sculpture; giclées and other reproductions are not accepted. Work must have been made in the last three years, must not have shown at the gallery before, may not exceed 40 inches in any direction including frame or base, and must be for sale for the run of the show, on which the gallery takes its standard 40% commission. Artists are responsible for shipping both ways and must include a prepaid return label. Up to six entries per artist at $40 for the first three and $5 for each additional. Notification August 24, work delivered September 8–12, and the exhibition runs September 19 – October 17, 2026, opening with a reception on September 19 at the gallery in Washington Depot, Connecticut. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $40 for up to 3 entries ($5 each additional). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Dezi Art Prize 2026
item.description: Two $1,000 unrestricted cash grants for early-career visual artists, run by Dezi, a career-support platform for artists launching in 2026. Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing and illustration, sculpture, filmmaking, design, UI/UX design, 2D/3D animation, fashion, and fiber and material arts. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over, one entry per artist per cycle, with no degree, gallery representation or exhibition history required. An independent jury of working arts professionals reviews every submission and scores it on four equally weighted criteria — quality of the work, originality and point of view, the artist statement, and the pitch for the grant — with jurors recusing themselves from any application where they know the applicant. Only the two winners receive cash; the top 30 ranked applicants are featured in Dezine, the platform's magazine, and get a named profile on the Dezi site, the top 20 of those also receive a free one-on-one career audit, and every applicant regardless of ranking is offered a post-close career-guidance interview. Winners agree to credit the prize on any new work made with the funds and to share the finished work within a year for possible inclusion in a future Dezi exhibition. Applications opened on 15 July, the jury reviews through September and winners are announced on 10 October 2026. The application fee is $30 flat with no added processing fees; the $20 early bird closed on 1 August 2026. The organisers offer a discount for students and will consider a waiver on request for anyone else for whom the fee is a barrier. Organised by Phistream LLC and led by founder Nitya Mehrotra, a RISD and SAIC graduate whose work spans animation, public art and gallery exhibition. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $1,000 x2.

item.title: International Artist Residency — Winter/Spring 2027 · bEam arts
item.description: One- or two-month studio residency in Thessaloniki, Greece, taking up to five artists from different disciplines per period. Applications for the winter/spring 2027 cycle close 24 August 2026 and decisions are confirmed by 4 September; the 2027 periods run monthly from January to July, and artists staying longer than a month can remain in the studios between periods. Each resident gets an individual studio in a shared space with their own key, continuous one-to-one mentorship and assistance, a well-equipped communal workshop, critiques, visits to museums, galleries and artist studios in Thessaloniki, the chance to propose site-specific projects, presentations or workshops, and a group exhibition at the end of each residency where work may be sold. Accommodation is optional. bEam arts is an independent, self-funded organisation that receives no external financial support, so the cost sits with the artist: €1,850 per month with accommodation or €1,000 per month without, duo artists €250 or €150 extra. There is no application fee; selected artists pay a deposit of 50% of the residence fee, refundable if cancelled 30 or more days before the start date. The organisers encourage applicants to seek funding from national arts councils, foundations or universities and will supply letters of invitation and acceptance and tailored wording for funding applications. Open to artists working in any medium; the application asks for an artist statement and a project proposal of up to 250 words each, plus a CV and 5 to 10 portfolio images with dimensions, technique, title and date. — Deadline: August 24, 2026. Fee: Free (€1,000–€1,850/month if selected). Prize: Residency.

item.title: Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant 2026
item.description: Printed Matter's annual programme of unrestricted grants for artists' book publishers, now in its third year and supported by the Wagner Foundation. In 2026 three grants of $10,000 each go to independent presses with a publishing history of one or more years, alongside a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair, with the table provided free of charge. The award is unrestricted: funds can cover production and development costs, artists' fees, equipment, studio rent or hired assistance, with no obligation to deliver a specific project. Eligible imprints should be small in scale and published with an independent spirit, without major ongoing distribution support; commercially run studios that only publish client work, and imprints attached to well-resourced institutions, are generally not eligible. The jury is broadly interested in presses that treat the book as a site for experimental artwork, that engage social and political themes with nuance, that give voice to marginalised perspectives, and that back emerging and underrepresented artists regardless of sales prospects. The grant is not aimed at artists seeking to fund a book of their own work, though artists who actively publish others are welcome. Open to publishers based anywhere; international applications encouraged. Past Publisher Work Grant winners cannot apply a second time. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × $10,000 + Art Book Fair table.

item.title: 1st Digital Art Exhibition · Philadelphia Sketch Club
item.description: The Philadelphia Sketch Club — founded in 1860 and the oldest artists' club in the United States — opens its first ever Digital Art Show, an open juried exhibition at its Camac Street galleries. Every submitted work must include a substantial amount of digitally created content, which suits composited, layered and heavily manipulated photo-based work; the club runs a separate annual PHOTOgraphy exhibition for straight photography and does not publish where the line between the two falls. Work must be original, not previously shown at the PSC, framed and wired for hanging, no larger than 24 inches in any dimension excluding the frame and no heavier than 30 lbs; prints deemed low-quality on delivery will not be hung. Artists may submit up to ten works, with a maximum of two accepted per artist. Works made with generative AI are not eligible in any PSC exhibition. Juror Perry Santulli selects the show, and prizes of $300, $200 and $100 are awarded with Contemporary Sketch Club Medals and certificates, plus at least three honourable mentions, presented at the reception on 11 October. All work must be for sale; the club takes 25% commission. The exhibition runs 4–25 October 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $25 + $10 per piece (members $10 + $10 per piece). Prize: $300 + Sketch Club Medal.

item.title: The Artist's Vision · MVA Gallery
item.description: National open call with no theme at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, filling both exhibition rooms. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are asked simply for their finest work — any theme, style or subject matter, traditional, experimental or a synthesis of the two — and the prospectus states plainly that all photographic processes are welcome. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works, with no cutoff date on when the work was made. The CaFE entry window runs 10 to 30 September 2026 — the prospectus text still prints an earlier August date the portal's own window overrides. Awards include an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery's second room, an optional $200 Director's Choice, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from every artist shown at the gallery during the year. Framed or gallery-wrapped work up to 48 inches, wired for hanging; plexiglass preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 24 January – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: 40 Over 40 · South x Southeast Photo Gallery
item.description: South x Southeast Gallery invites photographers over the age of 40 to enter its 40 Over 40 open call, curated by Elizabeth Avedon. The call is open to photographers of all backgrounds and experience levels, and all subject matter is welcome — street photography, portraits, nudes, landscapes, nature, wildlife, urban, architecture and documentary work. Selected photographs are shown in the gallery's online exhibition through September and October 2026, with a Zoom reception for the exhibiting photographers on a date to be announced. Entry is by email: images should be JPEG only, 72dpi and 1000 pixels on the longest side, named lastname-firstname-title (for example mccrarynancybigredhouse), zipped into a single file and attached to an email with the subject line '40 Over 40'. The entry fee is $40 for the first four images and $10 for each additional image, paid separately through the gallery's shop. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $40 for 4 images; $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: On Rose · Looking Glass Photographic Outfitters
item.description: Looking Glass, the independent photographic outfitters in Berkeley, launches On Rose to mark its move to a new home on Rose Street. Photographers are invited to interpret 'rose' as broadly as they like — as a flower, a colour, a symbol, a place, a story, an act of resistance or a moment of renewal. A rose does not need to appear in the picture, but the connection should be visible and meaningful. Each photograph is assigned to one of six categories: The Botanical Rose; Symbol, Story and Metaphor; Rose as Colour; Celebration, Honor and Community; On Rose Street; and They Rose Up. Entry uses a sliding-scale contribution of $5, $10, $15, $20, $25, $30, $40 or $50 — the amount chosen has no effect on judging, selection or awards — and one entry covers up to three photographs. Work is judged anonymously by Bay Area photographers Becky Jaffe, Sarah Deragon and Brandon Ruffin on interpretation of the theme (40%), visual voice and emotional resonance (40%) and photographic execution (20%). The overall winner, category winners and honourable mentions are exhibited at Abrams Claghorn Gallery & Shop in Albany, California in October 2026, with an opening reception; the overall winner also receives a commemorative trophy. Selected photographers are expected to be notified in October 2026. Photographs may be made on film, digital cameras or phones, and older work is welcome, but every entry must begin as a real-world capture by the entrant. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $5–$50 sliding scale. Prize: Exhibition at Abrams Claghorn Gallery + trophy.

item.title: (Not) Food Porn — From Feed to Culture · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, timed to the International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste on 29 September. The brief asks lens-based artists to work critically at the intersection of food imagery, consumption and culture: highly stylised "food porn" has reshaped how we perceive, desire and celebrate what we eat, and opposing feeds lean into raw, unedited aesthetics, while behind both sits massive global food waste and a rapidly shifting relationship to sustenance. Submissions are one project of up to 10 images, cohesive and not previously featured by Der Greif. Selected work is presented in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, and selected artists are invited into a small-group online roundtable critique facilitated by Der Greif staff as part of its Face-to-Face programme, with visibility across Der Greif's international community and a possible invitation to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio for sales and commissions. Selection is judged on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community. Der Greif describes this as a free submission with an optional €5 or €10 donation, but the Picter entry page carries a flat €10 fee; artists who cannot contribute financially can email the organiser for a 50% or 100% discount code. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: €10 (waivers available). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: 34th Tewksbury Juried Art Show · Tewksbury Historical Society
item.description: The Tewksbury Historical Society's juried art show returns for a 34th edition at the Zion Lutheran Christian Education Building in Oldwick, New Jersey, from 3 to 10 October 2026. Any two-dimensional media may be entered, photography explicitly included, with only giclees excluded; work on paper must be matted, framed, glazed and wired ready to hang. Each artist may enter up to five juried works, of which only one may reach 40 inches in any direction including frame. One $35 entry fee covers the juried entry and also opens the show's Small Works showcase (pieces up to 14 x 18 inches, priced at $500 or less) and its Portfolio showcase (up to ten works shown in a floor-standing print rack) at no extra charge. Six judging categories carry the awards: Animal Kingdom, Abstract/Non-Objective, Natural Environment, Figurative, Still Life/Florals and Built Environment. Show awards are $400 for Best in Show, $300 for Best of Tewksbury (a recognisable local building, site or scene) and the $200 Marion Katnack award for a Tewksbury landscape, with $125, $75 and $25 plus honourable mentions in each category. Artists are notified on 21 August, deliver work in person on 27 or 28 September, and collect unsold work on 10 October, with $25 a day charged on anything left unclaimed; the Society retains 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $400 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: MacDowell Fellowship — Spring/Summer 2027
item.description: MacDowell's Spring/Summer 2027 cycle, for residencies running March 1 – August 31, 2027 at the 450-acre estate in Peterborough, New Hampshire. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations and three prepared meals a day for up to eight weeks; there are no residency fees, and Fellows may apply for need-based stipends and travel reimbursement covering direct travel, rent, lost income and childcare. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, which MacDowell describes as spanning "photographers and printmakers to sculptors and creators of large-scale installation". The sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence and artists at any stage of practice may apply, but applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking program during the residency season and may submit only one application every 24 months; the reference-letter requirement is temporarily suspended. Applications open August 17, 2026. A $30 processing fee applies, with waivers available on request for financial hardship. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Funded residency up to 8 weeks.

item.title: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists 2027–28
item.description: The eighth iteration of the Queens Museum's fellowship for emerging visual artists living in the five boroughs of New York City. Two artists each receive $20,000, professional development consultations with QM staff, and four mentorship and feedback sessions over the year with an established New York artist of their choosing. Each fellowship runs one year and culminates in a solo project exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028; the award covers the artist fee, materials and production costs for the work made for that show. Emerging is defined as at least two but no more than ten years of practice outside a degree programme, with no solo exhibitions at established commercial galleries or museums and no major grants; age and formal training are not factors. Applications are reviewed by QM curatorial staff and two guest jurors, with in-person interviews for shortlisted candidates in November. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 × 2 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Brightwork Fellowship 2027
item.description: Anchorlight's flagship studio-based fellowship for one North Carolina artist a year at a pivotal moment in their career: a 500-plus square foot studio at Anchorlight in Raleigh, a solo exhibition in its zero-commission gallery, and an unrestricted award of $50,000. Anchorlight is home to 28 artist studios and a 1,500 square foot gallery; the Brightwork programme began in 2017 and relaunched under the current model in 2022, with the Brightwork Foundation formed in late 2025 to steward it. Applicants must have lived in North Carolina full time for at least twelve consecutive months and commit to staying for the fellowship. The same cycle also offers two Brightwork Grants to NC-based visual artists — a $2,000 Professional Development Grant and a $3,000 Studio Project Grant — but you may apply for only one of the three. Practising visual artists 21 and over of any career stage are eligible; performers, filmmakers, musicians and writers are not. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: $50,000 + studio + solo exhibition.

item.title: ON::View Artist Residency — February–May 2027
item.description: A fully funded residency in a street-level storefront studio at ARTS Southeast in Savannah's Starland District, where large east-facing windows let the neighbourhood watch the work happen around the clock. The residency provides free use of the 12-by-12-foot studio, free lodging at the nearby 5th Dimension Apartment and a $500 stipend that may go to travel, materials or anything the resident chooses, for an artist or curator making new work, continuing a project or doing research. Residents are encouraged to give a public lecture, workshop or other interactive event, and must work in the studio during ARTS Southeast's public open hours at least one day a week. Open internationally and to collaborative teams; artists may work in any medium suitable for the space, and current or recent ARTS Southeast studio members are not eligible. Programme partners include the SCAD Museum of Art and Telfair Museums. The $50 application fee can be waived on request if it is an undue burden. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Funded residency + $500 stipend.

item.title: SKOG Open Call 2027
item.description: SKOG, a cross-disciplinary exhibition space in Oslo dedicated to progressive contemporary art, photography and collectible objects, invites proposals for its 2027 exhibition programme. Both solo and group exhibition proposals are accepted, from emerging and established artists worldwide at any career stage and in any medium or technique. Applications are free and reviewed by SKOG's curatorial team; many of its exhibitions are developed collaboratively, so selected artists may be invited to show alongside others in a curated group presentation. Applications ask for a portfolio, CV, project description, and the materials, techniques and dimensions of the proposed work, against the gallery floor plan and its 2,750 mm ceiling height, and may be written in English or in Norwegian, Swedish or Danish. SKOG is seeking grant funding towards transport costs and artist fees but says it is unlikely to cover travel or accommodation in Oslo, and will discuss costs with shortlisted artists before deciding. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition at SKOG in 2027.

item.title: MY MICHIGAN: Our Rivers, Our Lakes · Grosse Pointe Artists Association
item.description: A juried themed exhibition at the Grosse Pointe Artists Association's gallery on The War Memorial campus in Grosse Pointe Farms, Michigan, asking artists to "prove the truth behind the slogan 'Water Wonderland' that was coined in 1963" — Michigan's rivers and lakes, however they are read. The juror is Alex Gilford, an artist and park ranger the association describes as noted for his efforts to strengthen the relationship between the arts and nature. Photography is one of the media the organisers accept, and the call's own banner image is a photograph, Donald Cronkhite's "Nankin Lake, After the Storm". Open to all artists over 18 and to alumni of GPAA's Promising Artists exhibitions; original work only, nothing made under an instructor, nothing previously exhibited with GPAA, and no large installation pieces. One to six pieces per artist, with the entry fee covering the first two and a $3 transaction fee added at checkout. There are no size limits, but 2D work must arrive framed and wired ready to hang; accepted work is delivered in person or shipped with a prepaid return label to the gallery on 26 September. Note two things before entering: the organisers publish no awards or prizes of any kind for this show — the return is the two-month hang — and work priced to sell carries a 35% gallery commission for members, 45% for non-members. Exhibition runs 1 October to 4 December 2026, with a gallery talk on the opening evening. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $40 / 2 pieces ($30 members) + $10 each addl. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Echoes of Fall 2026 · Medford Arts Center
item.description: All-media juried exhibition on fall-inspired work at the Medford Arts Center, a community arts centre on North Main Street in Medford, New Jersey. Michael Schweigart is juror of awards; chairs are Diane Emerson and Susan Barnes. Open to artists 18 and over, up to three original pieces each, none previously shown at MAC. Entry is $20 for the first work for members and $30 for non-members, plus $10 for each additional piece. Every accepted work goes into the online exhibition and into a brochure and YouTube video; artists who can hand deliver also have the option of showing their pieces in the gallery at 8 N. Main St. The show runs 4 September to 1 October 2026; artists are notified by email on 1 September, and the awards and online exhibit go up on 5 September. Cash awards for first place, second place and three honourable mentions, though the centre does not publish the amounts. All work must be for sale and Medford Arts takes 30% commission; artists ship sold work to the buyer themselves. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $30 first work ($20 members), $10 each extra. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Untitled — Carlotta Gallery
item.description: Carlotta Gallery's open-theme call, with no restrictions on subject, style or approach — the gallery says it welcomes photography projects that explore personal perspectives, stories and ideas through a distinctive visual language, and that Untitled "celebrates the freedom of expression and the many ways photographers interpret the world". Free to apply, pay only if selected; selected work is shown in a virtual exhibition for six to twelve months, permanently featured on the gallery's Collections page with a biography and artist statement, posted to @carlottagallery, and included in a free PDF exhibition catalogue, with a Certificate of Recognition. Open worldwide to photographers 18 and over; submit up to three JPEGs by email with a short biography and artist statement. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: Free (£20–£35 if accepted). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Standing on the Shoulders of the Ones Before Us · Clay Hand Studios
item.description: A juried gallery exhibition at Clay Hand Studios on Fresno's Gallery Row, built around the history and legacy of striving for freedom: demonstrations, resistance, solidarity, celebration and injustice, read as past, present and future chapters on the same path. Artists are invited to submit original work depicting people, events, artifacts, histories, hopes or consequences, and the brief is deliberately wide — "from realistic portrayals to imaginative interpretations" — welcoming personal as well as historical perspectives. Although Clay Hand is a ceramics studio, the call is not a ceramics call: the organisers state they encourage submissions in all visual art mediums "including painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, mixed media, digital art, and more", and photography is listed among the accepted media on the entry form alongside ceramic, multimedia, painting, fiber, sculpture and drawing. Work is judged by William Raines and Piet Ogata, and cash prizes are awarded in each category, though the organisers do not publish the amounts. The show runs 1–31 October 2026 at 660 Van Ness Avenue, timed to coincide with Fresno's Taste of Freedom Celebration. Entrants may submit one to three pieces, one entry per artist. AI-generated art is explicitly not accepted. NOTE ON WHO MAY ENTER: the organisers state both "Open to California artists" and, under the Eligibility heading, "Open to all artists" — the two lines sit side by side on their own page and on the entry form, so photographers outside California should confirm with the gallery before paying the fee. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: IMPACT: A Celebration of Photography · North Fork Arts Center
item.description: A free, blind-juried photography exhibition on the East End of Long Island, organised by a group of North Fork photographers and hosted in the gallery of the North Fork Arts Center, the 501(c)(3) nonprofit formed in 2023 to save the historic Greenport Theatre. Curators Paul Henry, an NFAC board member who previously ran a decade-long student film programme in Greenport, and Jeremy Garretson are looking for the photograph that stops you: not necessarily the technically perfect one, but the frame that holds a moment, reveals a beauty, or tells a story you cannot quite shake. The call is open to East End photographers of every experience level and age, professionals, enthusiasts, students and anyone who loves making pictures, and Henry has said he hopes it becomes the first step toward a broader photography programme for the community. Artists may enter up to three photographs of any subject, style or genre, made anywhere and at any time, each with a note of 100 words or fewer; there is no entry fee and images are reviewed blind, judged on overall impact and appeal alone. AI-generated or substantially AI-altered images are not eligible, though ordinary processing such as cropping, exposure and colour correction, dodging and burning, HDR blending, focus stacking and stitching is fine. Selected photographers supply a framed print in a black or white frame, no larger than 24 by 36 inches outside dimensions and wired for hanging, with assistance available to those who need it, and may add a sale price along with a website, gallery or portfolio link on the card beside the work. Entries close 24 August 2026, artists are notified 8 September, framed prints are due 8 October, and the exhibition opens with a public reception on Saturday 24 October, running to 22 November 2026. — Deadline: August 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photographers Without Borders Micro-Grants
item.description: A $500 USD micro-grant awarded to a different photographer every month by Photographers Without Borders, the nonprofit registered in both the US and Canada that has built its programme around ethical, community-rooted visual storytelling. Submissions take the form of a photo essay posted to PWB's members' community platform, and the brief is explicit about relationship: it is aimed at photographers with strong connections to the communities in their stories, whether they come from those communities themselves or have built those relationships over time. Subjects range across land and water protection, Indigenous science and wisdom, climate change and regeneration, and everything intersecting in between, including human rights, Indigenous sovereignty and land back. Mixed-media photographers are welcome. Recipients receive $500 USD. There is no submission fee, but applicants must be PWB members: basic membership is $9.99 a month and includes access to the community platform, the Storytelling for Change learning series and digital copies of the PWB magazine, and the organisation offers a needs-based membership to anyone who cannot afford it. Grants are awarded monthly on a rolling basis, so there is no fixed closing date. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free (PWB membership from $9.99/month). Prize: $500.

item.title: 49th Annual Photography Exhibit · Wassenberg Art Center
item.description: The Wassenberg Art Center's annual photography exhibition, now in its 49th year, hung in the centre's galleries in Van Wert, Ohio. Entries are juried across six subject categories — Nature (floral, wildlife, botanicals), Portraiture (including photojournalism), Architecture, Landscape (natural only), Abstract/Macro, and Film — with no more than two photographs per category and ten in total per photographer. The Film category asks for traditional analogue work and proof of negative may be requested. Awards run to $250 for Best of Show in Colour and another $250 for Best of Show in Black and White, plus seven $150 excellence awards, one per category and one for Youth Best of Show; the funds are administered by the Van Wert County Foundation. This is a physical, in-person exhibition: accepted work must reach the art center by the delivery deadline of 6 September 2026, and photographers outside driving distance may ship at their own cost both ways. Sales are handled by the art center, which takes a 30% commission. Work previously exhibited at the Wassenberg is not eligible, and no name, logo or title may be visible on the front of a print. Entries close 21 August 2026, jurying is announced 26 August, and the show runs 10 September to 8 October 2026. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $25 members / $35 non-members / $15 students (up to 10 images). Prize: $250 Best of Show + $150 category awards.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 75: Clay Every Which Way
item.description: The 75th issue of the UK independent art zine Haus-a-rest, edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers, takes clay as its subject — but explicitly not clay as pottery. The editors want work that goes beyond the pot, beyond tradition and beyond expectation: clay as unfired material, slip, earth pigment, digital simulation, or as a metaphor for transformation, identity, labour, geology, archaeology, ritual, play, memory and the body. Photography is named among the accepted media alongside sculpture, installation, painting, drawing, printmaking, textiles incorporating clay, mixed media, land art, performance documentation, video (YouTube links only) and digital works, and the call runs in parallel for writers submitting poetry, essays, short fiction, creative non-fiction and experimental texts. Conceptual responses are welcomed as warmly as material ones — the editors ask what it means to shape something with your hands, how clay remembers touch, and whether a material can carry history, culture or politics. Submit up to three artworks as JPEGs, or up to 1,000 words of writing, or a combination, together with titles, a statement of no more than 200 words explaining how the work fits the theme, and a biography of up to 150 words. An Instagram handle is required: selected contributors are asked to collaborate on sharing the posts. There is no submission fee, the call is open internationally to artists and writers at every career stage, and selected work is published in the online zine and gallery and promoted across the zine's social channels. Entry closes 3 September 2026 through CuratorSpace. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Forms and Fragments · Atlantic Gallery
item.description: The first annual online juried competition from Atlantic Gallery, the artist-run cooperative that has operated in Chelsea since 1974. Forms and Fragments asks artists to explore the relationship between what is transformed, remembered, assembled or broken, and the shapes those experiences become — the beauty of what remains, what is reconstructed and what emerges. Work may investigate memory, identity, landscape, culture, architecture, the body or abstraction through literal or symbolic fragments and evolving forms, considering how the parts relate to the whole, and the gallery invites personal, political, material and conceptual readings alike. The juror is Patricia Miranda, an artist, curator and educator who founded The Crit Lab and MAPSpace and the Lace Archive, and who has held residencies at the Textile Art Center, Vermont Studio Center, I-Park and Weir Farm. Photography is listed among the accepted media, alongside oils, acrylics, watercolours, pastels, drawings, traditional printmaking, original digital art, fibre art, mixed media and sculpture in any medium; digital or giclée reproductions of original artwork and AI-generated work are excluded. Entry is open to all artists 18 and over, at $30 for up to three works plus $10 for up to five more submitted at the same time, with no piece larger than 32 inches in any direction. Selected work is shown in an online exhibition running 1 October to 12 November 2026 and reproduced in an online digital catalogue, and every accepted piece is featured on the gallery's social channels. The award is the significant part: prize winners are selected for inclusion in Atlantic Gallery's physical group show in its Chelsea space, 1–19 December 2026, with work delivered in person or by proxy. The gallery takes 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 images), $10 for 5 more. Prize: Group exhibition in Chelsea, NYC.

item.title: Jazz Got Loose at The Gallery at the Attucks · Norfolk Arts
item.description: Norfolk Arts, the City of Norfolk's public arts agency, is filling the next six-month rotation at The Gallery at the Attucks, inside the historic Attucks Theatre in downtown Norfolk, Virginia — a 1919 building financed, designed and built by African Americans and one of the oldest surviving theatres of its kind in the United States. Jazz Got Loose treats jazz not only as a musical form but as a cultural movement rooted in New Orleans' Black communities and defined by freedom, resistance, identity and transformation. The call seeks work exploring liberation, resilience, social change, individuality and the courage to push against convention; politically charged, narrative-driven and culturally critical work is welcome, and Black artists and artists whose work reflects the cultural legacy of the Attucks are especially encouraged to apply. Delegate Jackie Hope Glass will jury the exhibition and select up to 50 original works. Any 2-D or relief visual medium is eligible, so photography qualifies, provided pieces do not exceed 50 pounds and arrive exhibition-ready with secure hanging hardware; video and digital work must come with its own display equipment. Artists must be 18 or over with a connection to Hampton Roads, and submit up to three images with title, medium, dimensions, year and a brief description of each work, a bio of up to 250 words and a statement of up to 300 words. There is no entry fee. Work may be offered for sale or marked not for sale, sales enquiries go straight to the artist, and Norfolk Arts takes no commission. The exhibition runs 29 October 2026 to 10 April 2027; artists deliver and collect their own work. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Six-month exhibition at the Attucks Theatre.

item.title: River Margin — Issue 1
item.description: River Margin is a new Australian and international literary journal founded in 2026 by the Melbourne-based visual artist, musician and writer Lana Eileen, and it is assembling its first issue. The focus is ecology, botany and wilderness: the journal was created as a space for overlooked aspects of the natural world — tiny wild-growing plants, threatened rivers, things hidden in the undergrowth. The name refers to the riparian zone, the natural border between water and land, and the editorial position follows from it: River Margin is a space where the liminal, the edge-dwelling, the peripheral and the unnoticed can find a voice. Photographers can submit up to seven images that relate in some way to ecology, botany, the environment, conservation or wilderness areas — rivers and bodies of water, insects, wildlife, fungi, plants, forests, mountains. Both digital and film photography are accepted; AI-generated work is not, and for visual art more broadly the journal excludes digital art as well. Files go by a file-sharing service such as WeTransfer to the journal's submissions address. Submissions are open worldwide and free, and the editors aim to respond within two weeks. The journal is candid that as a new publication compiling its first issue it is not in a position to pay contributors, so the return is publication in Issue 1 alongside poetry, essays, short fiction and creative non-fiction on the same themes. Submissions for the first issue close on 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in Issue 1.

item.title: Explorations: How We See Things · The Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center
item.description: The Norris Gallery's 2027 juried winter exhibition at the Dellora A. Norris Cultural Arts Center in St. Charles, Illinois. Explorations has no fixed subject: entries should reflect what engages the artist and inspires their exploration — of subject matter, of art processes, of media, or of point of view. Artists may submit up to three original works in any 2D or 3D medium or art process, which places photography squarely within scope; the only medium bar is on reproductions, so no giclées, and no work previously exhibited in the Norris galleries. The entry fee is $35 and is non-refundable. Monetary awards and honourable mentions are presented at the artists' reception. Accepted work cannot be shipped: it must be delivered in person by the artist or a representative on 4 January 2027 and collected on 15 February, which in practice limits the show to artists within reach of the Fox Valley. All accepted work must be for sale and must remain on display for the full run, with the centre retaining 30% commission on anything sold; accepted work may also be posted on the Norris Galleries website as well as hung in the gallery. Entries close on Monday 16 November 2026, artists hear back by Friday 11 December, and the exhibition runs 9 January to 14 February 2027. The Norris is a long-running community arts centre near Chicago with a performance hall and a gallery programme, and it runs a second annual juried show, Watercolor, on a separate cycle. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 works). Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Building Blocks: What Are We Building With? · St. Charles Arts Council
item.description: A blind-juried open call from the St. Charles Arts Council for an exhibition at its gallery in historic downtown St. Charles, Illinois. The premise is elemental: every creation begins with a single component, whether a stroke of paint, a block of wood or a spark of imagination, and the council asks how the individual components an artist chooses dictate the meaning of the final structure — for the artwork, for a life, or for a community. All art mediums are accepted and three-dimensional and assemblage work is actively encouraged, which leaves photography fully eligible. Artists may enter one or two pieces; the fee is $35 for non-members and $20 for council members, chosen from a tiered drop-down at entry. Work must be original, created within the last seven years, and never previously shown in a St. Charles Arts Council exhibit, and all entries must be for sale. Awards are presented at the opening reception, timed so that every participating artist can arrive: $150 for Best in Show, $75 for second place, $50 for third and further honourable mentions at the judge's discretion. Entries close 11 August 2026; work is dropped off on 31 August, the exhibition runs from early September to 25 October 2026 with an opening reception on the evening of 10 September, and pick-up is 26 October. The council notes it has no storage space, so artists unable to attend drop-off or collection must send someone in their place. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $35 ($20 members). Prize: $150 / $75 / $50 + Exhibition.

item.title: Petite Creations · Gresham Area League for the Arts
item.description: The Gresham Area League for the Arts' winter exhibition, hung in the Gresham Council Chamber Visual Arts Gallery in Oregon over the peak holiday season and mirrored in GALA's online galleries. The brief is scale: two-dimensional work must measure no more than 9 by 9 inches including the frame and no less than 5 by 5, and three-dimensional work must fit inside a 9-inch cube. Within that constraint the league is open across media and names photography directly alongside painting, drawing, mixed media, digital art, sculpture, pottery, fibre art and other 3-D work. Artists may enter up to three pieces for a single $30 submission fee, and GALA retains 20% commission on sales. Preference goes to artists in the greater Gresham area, though the league may widen the pool depending on the number of submissions; in practice the binding constraint is that artists must live within 30 miles of Gresham, because accepted work has to be delivered to the gallery in person. Work featuring nudity or sexual content is not accepted. Entries close 28 October 2026 and the exhibition runs 23 November 2026 to 8 January 2027. — Deadline: October 28, 2026. Fee: $30 (3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Presentations of Authorial Projects — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: The third of the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa's parallel open calls — alongside its photobook dummy exhibition and its self-publishing and small publishers space — this one offers photographers a speaking slot rather than a table. Selected authors present their own photobook project to fair visitors at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma, in sessions running across the fair: Friday 27 November between 5:30pm and 7:30pm, and Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November between 11:00am and 12:30pm and again from 2:00pm to 7:30pm. Each presentation runs a maximum of 25 minutes and a projector is available. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form and closes at 9:00pm on 12 October 2026; the fair's organisation confirms by 6 November whether the presentation will go ahead and at what time. There is no participation fee. The organisers note that authors whose project includes a photobook for sale should also register separately for the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores, and that dummies can be submitted in parallel for pre-selection in the dummy exhibition — the three calls share a deadline but are entered independently. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook presentation at the fair.

item.title: Small Works, Big Impact · The 203 Art Space
item.description: The 203 Art Space, a contemporary gallery and creative hub that opened in March 2026 on the 5th floor of the Stamford Town Center, invites submissions for its next monthly exhibition, "Small Works, Big Impact." The brief is bold pieces no larger than 24 x 24 inches that leave a lasting impression despite their scale — work where detail, colour, vibrancy and concept carry the memory. Photography is a named accepted medium alongside mixed media, digital, sculpture and painting. Artists may submit one to three pieces. All work must be wired and ready to hang; if stretcher bars are less than an inch and a half deep, the piece must be framed. Selections are announced 21 August and accepted work is dropped off in person at the gallery on 22 and 23 August. The show runs 26 August to 26 September 2026, with an opening reception on Saturday 29 August, 3–5pm. The gallery retains a 30% commission on work sold during the exhibition; the artist receives 70%. Entry is $40 for the first piece and $10 for each additional piece. Note that drop-off and pick-up are in person in Stamford, and no cash award is offered — the exhibition itself is the opportunity. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: $40 (1 piece) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: ANTHOLOGY 3 · Ephemere
item.description: ANTHOLOGY is Ephemere's cyclical curated group exhibition and publication series, and its third volume forms part of the Ephemere Photo Fest 2026 in Tokyo. Exactly nine artists are selected each round — "nine distinct petals of a single flower" — a number chosen so individual narratives complement rather than compete with one another across the gallery walls and the pages of an accompanying photobook. Applicants submit a portfolio of 15 to 20 images; the curatorial team, led by Ephemere founder Anne Murayama and assisted by Alfred Ong, then selects the nine final images that will represent each artist in both the show and the book. Ephemere handles all printing, layout design, framing and installation. ANTHOLOGY 3 runs 17–27 October 2026 on the 3rd floor of Three Space Tokyo. Applying is free, but selected artists pay a strictly non-refundable all-inclusive participation fee — ¥27,500 for Japan-based artists, $275 for visiting artists — covering the 11-day gallery placement, curatorial administration, professional printing and installation, and one complimentary copy of the photobook. Attendance is mandatory: proxy representation is not allowed and selected artists must be physically present in Tokyo on their designated Artist Talk day to give a 10–15 minute presentation alongside their work. Travel and accommodation are the artist's own cost. Two group video meetings in September cover logistics, and artists who join the take-down on 28 October may take their prints home free of charge. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: Free ($275 if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: Alongside its photobook dummy exhibition, the Lisbon Photobook Fair runs a Self-Publishing and Small Publishers Space — the Espaço dos Autores e Pequenos Editores — giving photographers who publish their own work, and the small presses that publish them, a place to sell at the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa, held 27–29 November 2026 at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico on Rua da Palma. The Authors' Space is managed by the fair's own organisation and asks a single one-off contribution rather than taking a cut: €10 covers up to two different titles and €20 covers three or four, in both cases with no limit on the number of copies you bring and, in the organisers' own words, no commission whatsoever on sales. Pre-registration is through a bilingual Portuguese/English Google Form submitted together with a maximum of six photographs of each photobook (72 dpi, 2 MB maximum, named for author and work) sent by WeTransfer to the fair under the subject 'Self-Publishers'. A registration only counts once the form, the images and the contribution have all been received. Pre-registration closes at 21:00 GMT on 12 October 2026, confirmations go out on 23 October, and books must reach the Arquivo Municipal by 16 November, delivered in person Monday to Saturday, 10am–6pm, or by post at the author's own cost; unsold copies are collected from the archive after the fair. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: €10 (up to 2 titles) / €20 (3–4 titles). Prize: Photobook fair sales space.

item.title: Emerald Renaissance: Celebrating 80 Years of Exhibiting Excellence · Philadelphia Chapter of The Links, Incorporated
item.description: A juried fine art exhibition marking the 80th anniversary of the Philadelphia chapter of The Links, Incorporated, the Black women's service organization founded in 1946. The theme asks how Black women — through friendship and service — have used the arts, education and cultural leadership to uplift communities across generations, and invites work that speaks to culture, history, connection and shared responsibility, interpreted through personal, cultural, historical or contemporary perspectives. Photography is explicitly among the eligible media, with painting, mixed media and works on paper. Open to artists living in Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery or Philadelphia counties, Pennsylvania; artists from historically underrepresented and underserved communities are strongly encouraged to apply, and emerging, mid-career and established artists are all welcome. Up to three works at $25 per entry; work must be original, made in the last three to five years, ready to install, at least 24 and no more than 36 inches wide and no more than 72 inches high. The jurors are Adrian J. Moody, gallerist and co-owner of Moody Jones Gallery; Rosalyn 'Roz' J. McPherson of The Roz Group, formerly Senior Vice President for the Science Center at The Franklin Institute; and Shelley R. Sylva, Head of Corporate Citizenship at TD Bank. Artists are notified 19 October 2026 and the exhibition is presented on 14 November 2026 at Founder's Hall, Girard College, alongside a live painting session and auction. All accepted work must be available for acquisition, with sales split 50/50 in favour of the artist; proceeds support the chapter's education, arts, health and mentorship programmes. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $25 per artwork. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Newhaven Open 26 · Photo Fringe
item.description: A new open exhibition from Photo Fringe, the volunteer-led Brighton charity behind the biennial open-platform photography festival, staged on the top floor of BN9 Marine Workshops in Newhaven — a working-waterfront studio space run by Towner with Newhaven Enterprise Zone and Lewes District Council, with almost 200 square metres of hanging space. Ten solo or group exhibitions will be selected, running 2 to 31 October 2026 alongside the rest of the festival. Work should respond to the 2026 festival theme Feedback Loop, which asks artists to treat photography less as a static record than as part of a continuous exchange: conversations between communities and landscapes, stories circulating across generations, ecological cycles, industrial systems, acts of collaboration, the shifting relationship between artists and audiences. It should also connect meaningfully to Marine Workshops, Newhaven or its communities — the call is open to photographers and lens-based artists in any medium, including installation, moving image, sound and expanded photographic practice, and site-responsive proposals for new or existing work are both welcome. Collectives may apply. Apply free by email with up to 300 words on the proposal, up to 12 JPEGs or a screener link, and a website or Instagram link; BSL, English audio and video applications are accepted. One exhibiting artist receives a jury award of mentorship with Photo Fringe producer Ricardo Reverón Blanco plus an in-depth interview published on the festival site. Selected artists install and de-install their own work with team support, invigilate for at least a day, and pay the subsidised registration fee of £125 solo or £150 group plus a £100 contribution towards exhibition costs by 2 September; Photo Fringe takes 35% commission on sales to cover staffing. Entries close 11.59pm on Sunday 23 August 2026, with notifications on 28 August. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: Free (£125 solo / £150 group registration + £100 exhibition contribution if selected). Prize: Exhibition + Mentorship.

item.title: Medium Gallery Open Call 2027
item.description: Medium Gallery was founded on 8 January 1991 as part of the Academy of Fine Arts and Design in Bratislava, and its programme spans every form of contemporary art the school teaches — photography, painting, intermedia, graphic design, sculpture, applied arts, architecture, design, restoration, textiles and visual communication. For 2027 it is again inviting exhibition projects from students of art fields, beginning and established artists, and curatorial projects, from Slovakia and abroad; the gallery board deliberately balances student presentations against shows by established local and international artists. The 173-square-metre space can be partitioned, a practice begun by former gallery head Jana Kapelová in 2018, so applicants choose one of three configurations: SMALL, the back room, best for compact solo shows; MEDIUM, the two front rooms, for a solo or smaller group show; or LARGE, the whole gallery. Proposals are assessed by a five-person board of three school representatives, the gallery manager and one external member. The gallery covers the space and its running costs, invigilation, technical equipment, plinths and basic installation supplies, transport of works by agreement, graphic design and a print run of posters in the gallery's visual identity, press and social media, photographic documentation of the opening and installation views, the opening itself, and partial help installing; artists cover opening refreshments, their own installation labour, any equipment the gallery cannot supply, and returning the space to its prior state. Applications are free and go by email to the gallery, with a short and detailed project description, chosen space, CVs, an artist portfolio as a single PDF, a preferred exhibition date, an installation plan and any accompanying programme. Final bachelor's and master's theses are not eligible. The deadline is Sunday 16 August 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: International Mute Photo Festival 2027 — Nature Ate the Pixels · Photonisos Arts & Culture
item.description: Photonisos Arts & Culture, the Samos non-profit behind the East End – Samos Arts Festival, is launching the first International Mute Photo Festival with a single, uncompromising rule: every photograph must be captured and printed on a children's instant thermal camera — the cheap toy that spits low-resolution black-and-white images onto thermal paper. The festival frames this as a deliberate subversion, taking Guy Debord's warning about a world replaced by its own images and answering it with a medium too coarse to flatter anything. The theme, Nature Ate the Pixels, asks for work in which human presence sits inside the natural world rather than above it, split across four categories: Landscape (nature with no human trace), Symbiosis (the body meeting water, earth and flora), Rebirth (nature reclaiming the cityscape) and Future (children discovering the natural world). Post-processing is almost entirely forbidden — you may crop the printed timestamp and white borders and convert to black and white, and nothing else; the lines, marks and noise of the thermal print are treated as the work's core identity, not as faults. Entrants submit high-resolution scans of their original prints, and the jury may ask to see the physical strips to verify the medium. Fifteen adult series and five from the under-18 category are selected, printed and enlarged entirely at the festival's expense, published in a printed catalogue, and shown in July 2027 at the renovated Old Customs Warehouses at Karlovasi Port on Samos. The artist behind the most complete series gets travel and accommodation covered for the opening. Entry is free, and artists retain full copyright. Submissions open 1 September 2026 and close 30 April 2027 at 23:59 EEST; adults send 6 to 9 images with a 250-word statement by email as a single ZIP, and under-18 entries of 5 images must come from a parent or guardian's address with a written consent declaration in the body of the email. — Deadline: April 30, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Food: Ritual and Identity · Metchosin ArtPod
item.description: The artist-run ArtPod on southern Vancouver Island closes its 2026 season with a show about what feeds us. Food is never just food, the curators write — it is material, metaphor, ritual and resource, and it feeds identities, cultures, economies and memories as much as bodies. The call asks for work that traces the visible and invisible systems that sustain or exploit us, from harvest to hunger and feast to waste, and treats food as personal, political, ecological and sensual at once. The guiding question is what it means to be nourished in a time of both abundance and imbalance. The curatorial team is Anna Mar, Pierrette Vezina and Cindy McMath, with Janice Beaudoin jurying. Photography is explicitly welcome under the ArtPod's standing submission guidelines: limited-edition photographs and prints, including giclée, inkjet and archival prints, are accepted in editions of 25 or fewer, and photographs must be taken by the artist and may not reproduce another artist's work. On AI the ArtPod says it is still reflecting, but requires submitted work to represent the artist's own creative vision and authorship. Jurying is blind — the juror sees only the image, the medium and substrate, and an artist statement capped at 1,000 characters. Artists may submit up to three original works; diptychs, triptychs and small series count as one work if shown in a single photograph. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 7 feet high by 5 feet wide. Work must not have been shown in a juried exhibition or commercial gallery on southern Vancouver Island in the past year. Submission is CA$10 per artwork with a further CA$20 hanging fee per accepted work; the ArtPod takes 30% commission and all work must be for sale. The call runs 12 August to 9 October with results on 12 October, and the exhibition runs 23 October to 20 December 2026 with an opening gala on 24 October, 2–4 pm. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: CA$10 per work (CA$20 more if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Truth in Art: A Juried Opportunity for MFA Students · Steffen Thomas Museum of Art
item.description: The Steffen Thomas Museum of Art is a single-artist museum — one of only fourteen in the United States by its own count — built around the work of German-born American painter and sculptor Steffen Thomas. Through its College Connections programme the museum runs this free juried exhibition for MFA students, and the point is as much the apprenticeship as the wall space: selected students work alongside museum mentors on curating, loan forms and condition reports, art installation, exhibition promotion and public speaking, so the show doubles as a first practical education in how a museum actually mounts an exhibition. The top three Best in Show selections receive a monetary award. Entry is free. Submissions close 29 August 2026 and the exhibition runs 26 September to 21 November 2026 in the museum's West Gallery in Buckhead, Georgia, in Morgan County about ten minutes from historic Madison. — Deadline: August 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: PLAYFUL · Arc Studios & Gallery
item.description: Arc is a mixed-use art centre on Folsom Street in San Francisco's South of Market district, founded in 2010 by four artist partners and running three galleries alongside ten artist studios. Its 2027 national juried call opens with Claes Oldenburg — "I am for the art of the underwear and the art of taxicabs" — and asks for work that embodies the playful spirit: light-hearted, lively, spontaneous, full of fun, amusement and wit. That can arrive as bright colour, whimsical typography, funny imagery or sly innuendo, and the gallery specifically names spontaneous street photography alongside interactive works that invite audience participation and works that hold on to child-like wonder and game-play. Photography is one of the accepted categories; jewellery, video, film, performance, installation and anything needing an external power source are not. The juror is Jennifer Farris, who has run STUDIO Gallery in San Francisco with her husband, artist Rab Terry, for over two decades. Three works chosen by the juror for the most imaginative reading of the theme receive a $250 check, a juror's award ribbon, a recognition certificate and the show catalogue; every selected work, gallery and online alike, appears in that catalogue. Entry is $35 for one to three images, with a maximum of two entries per artist, and the call is open to artists residing in the United States. Two-dimensional work is capped at 60 by 40 inches including frame, and accepted work must arrive ready to hang with plexi rather than glass. Submissions close 29 March 2027, notifications go out 16 April, and the exhibition runs 19 June to 17 July 2027 at 1246 Folsom Street. — Deadline: March 29, 2027. Fee: $35 per entry (1–3 works). Prize: $250 awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Living Image 2026/2027 · The Halide Project
item.description: The Halide Project is a nonprofit darkroom and gallery on North 2nd Street in Philadelphia, and Living Image is its annual juried exhibition of traditional and historic photographic processes — the show it builds its year around. The 2026/27 edition is juried by Amanda Smith, who founded A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas fifteen years ago and has run more than 200 juried and curated exhibitions there, alongside jury work for All About Photo, Analogue Forever, Dodho, Texas Photographic Society, the International Photography Hall of Fame and Critical Mass. Selected work hangs at The Halide Project gallery from 5 December 2026 to 17 January 2027 and is published in a printed catalogue; every selected artist receives a copy. One Grand Prize winner takes $250 and a slot to show a body of work in The Halide Project's annual Spring Invitational, with further sponsored prizes announced later. The medium gate is strict and specific: work must be made using traditional, pre-digital photographic printing — silver gelatin, c-prints, instant film, platinum/palladium, cyanotype, gum bichromate, wet plate collodion and other alternative and historic processes. Analog prints made from digital negatives are eligible; inkjet prints and digital c-prints are not, even if shot on film. Open to artists 18 or older in any country. Entry is $40 for up to three works and $10 for each additional, to a maximum of ten, with a $5 discount off the total for members. Accepted work must arrive framed and wired to professional standards by 7 November and must not exceed 30 inches in any dimension including the frame; artists cover shipping both ways, and the gallery retains a 25% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $40 (1–3 works), $10 each additional. Prize: $250 + Exhibition + Printed catalogue.
